src_members.sig: public static void DestroyChildren(this Transform t)
src_members.name: DestroyChildren
src_members.comment: Destroys every child under a transform, e.g. clearing a spawned-items container before repopulating it. The naive version — just calling Object.Destroy on each child — reads as if the container is empty afterwards, but Unity DEFERS Destroy to the end of the frame: childCount is unchanged on the very next line, and a container you clear and refill in the same Update ends up holding both sets. Each child is therefore DETACHED first, which takes effect immediately, so the container really is empty as soon as this returns; the orphaned objects are then destroyed on Unity's normal schedule. Outside Play mode Destroy never runs at all, so DestroyImmediate is used there instead.
